leif-erikson.name: Leif Erikson
leif-erikson.bio: Son of Erik the Red, who founded the first Norse settlement in Greenland, he was raised there. The Icelandic sagas have him reach Vinland, usually read as the coast of North America, about half a millennium before Columbus; the Norse site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland may be his. After his father died he led the Greenland settlement.

images.author: Christian Krohg
images.note: No likeness survives; a Norwegian painting of nine centuries later.

born.label: Leif Erikson born in Iceland, c. 970s
born.text: The sagas do not say where. Iceland, where his parents met, is the likeliest country, and Haukadalur, his mother's family's valley, the usual guess; the mark stands at Eiríksstaðir, the farm there.

death.label: Leif Erikson died, c. 1020, probably at Brattahlíð
death.text: The sagas are silent. He is last named alive about 1018–19 and his son Thorkell held the chieftaincy by 1025; Brattahlíð, the family estate, is the likeliest place.
death.source: Leif Erikson (Wikipedia): no saga records his death

marco-polo.name: Marco Polo
marco-polo.bio: A Venetian merchant who set out with his father Niccolò and uncle Maffeo in 1271 and reached the court of Kublai Khan, who sent him on missions across the empire and beyond. He was back in Venice in 1295. His Travels, written down about 1300, gave Europe its first broad look at China, Persia and India.

images.author: Maître de la mazarine et collab.
Unknown
images.note: A woodcut on the first German edition of his book, a century and a half after his death.

born.label: Marco Polo born at Venice, c. 1254
born.text: Born about 1254 in Venice; no document of the time records the day.
born.doubt: Korčula, an island off the Dalmatian coast, says he was born there and shows visitors a house it calls his; others have put his birth in Constantinople.

death.label: Marco Polo died at Venice, 8 Jan 1324
death.text: He died at home in January 1324. His will freed Peter, his Tatar slave. Priests are said to have urged him on his deathbed to take back his Book; he answered that he had not told the half of what he saw.

ibn-battuta.name: Ibn Battuta
ibn-battuta.bio: A scholar and judge from Tangier who spent about thirty years, 1325 to 1354, travelling through much of Africa, Asia and Iberia, by most counts farther than any other traveller before modern times. Near the end of his life he dictated the account known as the Rihla.

images.author: Ibn Juzayy; Bibliothèque nationale de France
Léon Benett
images.note: No likeness survives; an illustration for Jules Verne's Découverte de la terre, five centuries after his death.

born.label: Ibn Battuta born at Tangier, 24 Feb 1304
born.text: The day comes from his own account in the Rihla.

death.label: Ibn Battuta died in Morocco, c. 1369
death.text: He dictated the Rihla at Fez in 1355–56 and died in Morocco about 1368–69. Nobody recorded where, so the skull stands in the country, not on a town.

alternatives.label: Died at Marrakesh, by one modern account
alternatives.text: Some modern summaries put his death at Marrakesh; the Rihla ends in 1355 and no chronicle of his death survives. The tomb shown at Tangier, his birthplace, is purported, and marks a burial tradition, not a place of death.
alternatives.source: Wikipedia, Ibn Battuta (infobox); the Tangier tomb is captioned "purported"

zheng-he.name: Zheng He
zheng-he.bio: Born Ma He to a Hui Muslim family in Yunnan, he served the Yongle Emperor, who gave him the name Zheng. Between 1405 and 1433 he commanded seven treasure voyages across the Indian Ocean as far as the Swahili coast, and he served as commander of the southern capital, Nanjing.

images.author: Mao Yuanyi, Wubei Zhi, and an unknown cartographer
Unknown
images.note: Published about 1600 in a fictionalised account of his voyages.

born.label: Zheng He born in Yunnan, 1371
born.text: Born Ma He to a Hui family of Kunyang, Kunming, then held for the Northern Yuan. The mark stands on Kunming.

death.label: Zheng He died at sea on the way home, 1433
death.text: Most accounts have him die in 1433 on the way home from the seventh voyage, some say buried at sea. None gives a place, so the skull stands mid-way along that voyage's Calicut–Malacca leg.
death.source: Zheng He (Wikipedia); no source gives the place

alternatives.label: Died at Calicut on the way home, 1433
alternatives.text: On the seventh voyage the fleet called at Calicut on its way back from Hormuz. Some historians have him die there, before it sailed for Malacca.

alternatives.label: Home at Nanjing, died 1435
alternatives.text: A minority view, from later texts and inscriptions, has him live two years more. A tomb is shown at Nanjing.
alternatives.source: Zheng He (Wikipedia); the later Nanjing account

bartolomeu-dias.name: Bartolomeu Dias
bartolomeu-dias.bio: A Portuguese mariner, in February 1488 he became the first European to round the southern tip of Africa, and showed that the way south lies well out to sea, southwest of the African coast. Vasco da Gama used what he found to reach India.

images.author: RedCoat; cut by Biser Todorov
images.note: No likeness survives; a photograph of his statue at South Africa House, London.

death.label: Dias lost in a storm off the Cape, on Cabral's fleet, 1500
death.text: Four of Cabral's ships went down in one storm on the way to the Cape. The wreck's position is not recorded; the skull stands off the Cape.

christopher-columbus.name: Christopher Columbus
christopher-columbus.bio: A Genoese navigator who went to sea young, sailed as far as the British Isles and the Gold Coast, and lived some years in Lisbon. Sponsored by the Catholic Monarchs, he left Palos in August 1492 and made landfall in the Americas on 12 October; he made four Spanish crossings in all.

images.author: Sebastiano del Piombo
images.note: Said to be him; the sitter is not proven, and no authenticated portrait exists.

born.label: Columbus born at Genoa, between Aug and Oct 1451
born.text: Born between 25 August and 31 October 1451 in the Republic of Genoa.
born.doubt: Calvi in Corsica still marks a house as his birthplace, and Catalans, Galicians and Portuguese have each argued he was one of their own.

death.label: Columbus dies at Valladolid
death.text: He died in a rented house, ill, still arguing that the Crown owed him the titles and the tenth of the profits it had promised. He is generally said to have held that he had reached the edge of Asia. His bones were carried to Seville, then Santo Domingo, then Havana, then Seville again, and Seville and Santo Domingo both still claim him.

juan-de-la-cosa.name: Juan de la Cosa
juan-de-la-cosa.bio: Owner and master of the Santa María on the first voyage, pilot on later ones, and maker of the oldest surviving chart to show the New World, in 1500.

born.label: Juan de la Cosa born at Santoña, c. 1450–1460
born.text: No record of his birth survives; Santoña is the usual account, and the years are read back from his career.

death.label: Juan de la Cosa killed near Turbaco, 1510
death.text: Sailing as pilot to Alonso de Ojeda on the coast of what is now Colombia, he went ashore with a raiding party near Turbaco and was killed by the townspeople's poisoned arrows.

paulo-da-gama.name: Paulo da Gama
paulo-da-gama.bio: Vasco da Gama's elder brother, a son of Estêvão da Gama and Isabel Sodré, he commanded the São Rafael on the first voyage to India. She was scuttled on the way home and he went over to the São Gabriel. He fell ill; his brother took him to Terceira in the Azores and stayed with him until he died. He is buried at Angra do Heroísmo.

images.author: Francisco Pastor Muntó
images.note: A newspaper portrait four centuries after his death.

death.label: Paulo da Gama died at Angra, Terceira
death.text: Paulo commanded the São Rafael, burned on the East African coast when there were too few men left to sail her. He fell ill on the way home; Vasco sailed on ahead in a fast caravel, to hurry him to the Azores, and stayed with his brother until he died.

vasco-da-gama.name: Vasco da Gama
vasco-da-gama.bio: A Portuguese nobleman from Sines, on his first voyage, 1497 to 1499, he found the sea road from Europe to India, round the Cape of Good Hope and across the Indian Ocean from Malindi to Calicut, the longest ocean voyage made until then. He went back to India as viceroy and died there in 1524.

images.author: Gregório Lopes
images.note: Painted about the year he died.

images.author: unknown master of the Portuguese School

born.label: Vasco da Gama born at Sines, c. 1460s
born.text: Born at Sines, a seaport on the Alentejo coast; some give about 1460, others 1469.

death.label: Vasco da Gama died at Cochin as Viceroy of India
death.text: Sent back to India at last as viceroy, he fell ill within months of landing and died at Cochin on Christmas Eve. His body was taken to Portugal in 1539, and lies today in the Jerónimos Monastery at Lisbon.

ferdinand-magellan.name: Ferdinand Magellan
ferdinand-magellan.bio: A Portuguese officer of minor nobility who served the Crown in Asia, then, refused by King Manuel, took his plan to sail west to the Moluccas to Charles I of Spain. He led the 1519 expedition through the strait that bears his name and across the Pacific, and was killed at Mactan in 1521; Elcano brought the Victoria home in 1522.

images.author: Unknown
images.note: A copy after the portrait in the Naval Museum, Madrid; no authenticated likeness exists.

born.label: Magellan born in northern Portugal, c. 1480
born.text: Born in northern Portugal, possibly around 1480. The mark stands on Sabrosa, where the family house stood.

alternatives.label: Born at Ponte da Barca, by another account
alternatives.text: Wikidata gives Ponte da Barca beside Sabrosa as his birthplace.

death.label: Magellan killed at Mactan
death.text: Magellan took sides in a local quarrel, for the Cebu king against Lapulapu of Mactan, and went ashore with about fifty men. The ships' guns could not reach the beach, the Mactan fighters came on in waves, and the captain-general was killed in the water. Pigafetta, who was there, called him "our mirror, our light, our comfort and our true guide".

juan-sebastian-elcano.name: Juan Sebastián Elcano
juan-sebastian-elcano.bio: A Basque ship-owner from Getaria, he brought the Victoria home in 1522, the first ship round the world, after choosing to go on west across the Indian Ocean against his orders to return by the Pacific. Charles V gave him arms with a globe and Primus circumdedisti me. Sent out again under Loaísa, he died of scurvy in the Pacific in 1526. Little is known of his private life.

images.author: Unknown
images.note: Museo Naval, Madrid; painted three centuries after him.

born.label: Elcano born at Getaria, 1486 or 1487
born.text: His own will names Getaria. The year comes from his saying, in August 1519, that he was "approximately" 32.

death.label: Elcano died at sea on the Loaísa expedition, 1526
death.text: He took command when Loaísa died days before, and died himself at sea in early August, in mid-Pacific near the equator; accounts give the 4th, 5th or 6th. No position is recorded, so the skull stands on the equator mid-ocean.

francis-drake.name: Francis Drake
francis-drake.bio: Born in Devon and raised in the Plymouth household of William Hawkins, he sailed on his cousin John Hawkins's slaving voyages and raided the Spanish Main. From 1577 to 1580 he made the second voyage round the world, the first English one, and was knighted aboard the Golden Hind. He was vice admiral against the Armada in 1588.

born.label: Drake born at Tavistock, c. 1540
born.text: Born at Crowndale Farm, Tavistock; the year is reckoned, and accounts differ.

death.label: Drake died off Portobelo, 1596; buried at sea in a lead coffin
death.text: Dysentery killed him on his last raid on the Spanish Caribbean. Drake asked to be dressed in his armour, and was buried at sea in a lead coffin off Portobelo. Divers still look for it.

phoenician-mariners-of-necho-ii.name: Phoenician mariners of Necho II
phoenician-mariners-of-necho-ii.bio: Herodotus tells that Necho II of Egypt (610–595 BC) sent out Phoenicians who sailed from the Red Sea round Africa to the Strait of Gibraltar and back to Egypt in three years. Nobody named them.

hanno-the-navigator.name: Hanno the Navigator
hanno-the-navigator.bio: A Carthaginian, sometimes called a king, who sailed down the coast of West Africa in the fifth century BC. Only a Greek periplus tells of it, and nobody agrees how far he went: some say Gabon, others no farther than southern Morocco.

born.label: Hanno of Carthage, 5th century BC
born.text: Nothing is known of his birth. He was a Carthaginian who lived in the fifth century BC, so the mark stands on Carthage.

pytheas.name: Pytheas
pytheas.bio: A Greek of Massalia who sailed to northern Europe about 325 BC, round much of the British Isles, and was the first on record to describe the midnight sun and polar ice. He gave the world Thule, and first tied the tides to the moon. His own book is lost; he survives in quotation by later writers.

images.author: Mellangoose
images.note: No likeness exists. The page of the oldest manuscript of Strabo (10th century) that quotes him, the text he survives in.

born.label: Pytheas born at Massalia, c. 350 BC
born.text: Known only through later writers who quote him; the year is a reckoning from when he flourished.

nearchus.name: Nearchus
nearchus.bio: A Cretan whose family settled at Amphipolis in Macedonia; one of Alexander's boyhood friends and his navarch. In 326–324 BC he led the fleet from the Indus along the coast and up the Persian Gulf to the mouth of the Tigris.

images.author: André Castaigne
images.note: Alexander's fleet on the Indus as a 19th-century illustrator saw it; not a likeness of Nearchus.

born.label: Nearchus born on Crete, c. 360 BC
born.text: A native of Lato, son of Androtimus, whose family moved to Amphipolis while he was a boy; so he was quite possibly born on Crete.

death.label: Ponce de León died in Cuba, July 1521
death.text: A Calusa arrow struck his thigh on his 1521 attempt to colonise south-west Florida, and he died in the first week of July, probably of infection, soon after the expedition sailed to Cuba; he was buried in Puerto Rico. The page names no town, so the mark stands at Havana, the port the expedition made for, an editorial guess.

death.label: Juan Garrido died in Mexico City, between 1547 and 1550
death.source: NPS, Juan Garrido: from legal documents
death.text: NPS dates his death between 1547 and 1550 from legal documents; Wikipedia says about 1550, in New Spain. His burial place is unknown.

death.label: Narváez lost at sea, 1528
death.text: He is believed to have been swept out to sea in a storm while the boats worked west along the Gulf coast; nobody recorded where. The skull stands at the middle of the boat leg, and the place is only inferred.

death.label: Cabeza de Vaca died in Spain, on an uncertain date
death.source: Wikipedia, Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca
death.text: His last surviving record is dated 19 May 1559. He died on an uncertain date, at Jerez de la Frontera or at Valladolid.

alternatives.label: Died at Valladolid, by the other account
alternatives.source: Wikipedia, Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca

death.label: Esteban killed at Hawikuh, 1539
death.text: He went ahead of Fray Marcos de Niza and was held overnight without food or water, then attacked and killed at Cíbola. The Zuni may have thought him a bad man; Castañeda says he asked for turquoise and women; Alarcón says he boasted of armed men behind him; Sancho Dorantes says he was shot through with arrows.
death.doubt: In 2002 the historian Juan Francisco Maura argued that Esteban was never killed at all: the story of his death was a ruse that set a slave free, and he lived on among the Zuni.

mansa-musa.name: Mansa Musa
mansa-musa.bio: Mansa, or king, of Mali from about 1312 to about 1337. On his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324–25 he spent three months in Cairo and gave away and spent so much gold that, by al-Umari's report, its price there had not recovered twelve years later. European charts drew him within years: Dulcert's of 1339 names him, and the Catalan Atlas of 1375 sets him on a throne holding up gold. Under him part of the Djinguereber Mosque was built at Timbuktu, and the city grew into a centre of Islamic learning. In Cairo he told a story of how he came to the throne: the mansa before him, he said, had sailed west into the Atlantic with a great fleet and never came back. Siphiwe Baleka of the Balanta Society writes that Mali's wealth came from taxes, trade and enslavement, and that peoples such as the Balanta, who refused its taxes and its rule, remember it as an empire that raided them.

images.author: Attributed to Abraham Cresques
images.note: Sheet 6 of the Catalan Atlas: Musa on a throne, holding a gold coin. Drawn about forty years after his death, from report rather than sight, it is the only medieval picture of him.

born.text: Nobody recorded when or where he was born; c. 1280 is a modern estimate, and the place is given only as the Mali Empire.

death.text: The date is uncertain: estimates run from about 1332 to 1337, and Levtzion thought 1337 the likeliest. Nobody recorded where, so no skull is drawn.

abu-bakr-ii.name: The mansa before Musa
abu-bakr-ii.bio: The king of Mali before Mansa Musa, known only from Musa's own account, told in Cairo in 1324 and written down by al-Umari: he wished to find the far edge of the Atlantic, sent out a fleet of which one ship came back, then sailed himself with a greater one, leaving Musa to rule in his place, and was never seen again. His name is not certain. Al-Umari gives none; Ibn Khaldun, writing decades later, names Musa's predecessor as Muhammad ibn Qu, and the historians who take the voyage seriously mostly attribute it to him; a few suggest instead his father Qu, the mansa before Muhammad. The name Abu Bakr II, by which he is popularly known, comes from a nineteenth-century mistranslation of Ibn Khaldun. No other medieval Arab historian and no West African oral tradition tells of the voyage. Some historians take it seriously; others suspect that Musa deposed his predecessor and told of the voyage to justify his rise.

death.text: No death is recorded. In Musa's telling he sailed west with his fleet and was never seen again; where, or whether he sailed at all, nobody knows, so no skull is drawn.

erik-the-red.name: Erik the Red
erik-the-red.bio: A Norwegian-born chieftain settled in Iceland, outlawed for killings there about 982. He spent his three years of exile finding and naming Greenland, then came back to Iceland and led the first settlers across. He was the father of Leif Erikson.

born.label: Erik the Red born in Norway, c. 950
born.text: The sagas say he came from Jæren, in south-west Norway, and that his father Thorvald fled to Iceland. The mark stands on that district, and the year is a guess.

death.label: Erik the Red died, c. 1003, probably at Brattahlíð
death.text: The saga has him die of an epidemic in Greenland after Leif's return. He was buried in the country he named; the mark stands at his farm.

bjarni-herjolfsson.name: Bjarni Herjólfsson
bjarni-herjolfsson.bio: An Icelandic merchant whose father had gone with Erik to Greenland. Sailing after him in 986 without chart or compass, he was blown off course and became the first European recorded to see the coast of North America, though he never landed. The Saga of the Greenlanders has Leif Erikson buy his ship and follow his sightings.
